newsitem.title: LEBANON: VIOLENCE FUELS DOLLAR DEMAND IN LEBANON.
newsitem.headline: VIOLENCE FUELS DOLLAR DEMAND IN LEBANON.

text.p: The central bank moved to satisfy dollar demand fuelled by violence in south Lebanon this week, dealers said on Friday.
The Bank of Lebanon's bid-offer intervention band was 1,532.50-1,541.50 Lebanese pounds compared to last week's 1,533.00-1,542.00, continuing its recent rate of officially sanctioned appreciation.
Dealers said the U.S. decision to end on July 31 a 10-year-old ban on its citizens travelling to Lebanon had boosted the Lebanese pound.
But they said this week's violence in south Lebanon, the worst since a major Israeli offensive over a year ago, had strengthened the dollar.
"There were some fears of an Israeli (military) operation. This had an impact on the market," said one dealer.
In interbank trading, dealers said interbank trading was in a range of 1,535.00-1,541.50 against last week's 1,538-1,539. -- Beirut editorial (9611) 745307 745308
